intro.title: Flex: container and direction
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage layout using CSS Flexbox to arrange elements in a row or column. You will learn the core concept of the flex container, which controls the alignment and direction of its child items. The main technologies involved are CSS properties like 'display: flex' and 'flex-direction'. By the end, you'll understand how to create flexible layouts that adapt to different screen sizes and content.
intro.usecase: Flexbox container and direction properties are fundamental for creating modern, responsive layouts in real-world interfaces. Developers use these daily when building navigation menus that need to align horizontally, arranging form controls in logical rows or columns, or organizing dashboard panels that adapt to different screen sizes. For example, a product filter sidebar with stacked checkboxes uses flex-direction: column, while a horizontal tab navigation uses flex-direction: row. Understanding these core flex concepts allows you to create predictable, maintainable layouts for components like card grids, modal footers, and responsive toolbars that work consistently across devices.
